title: Quantifying Natural Hydrogen‐Helium Sources and Dynamic Accumulation in Global Sedimentary Basins
content:
Abstract

Despite the scientific and economic importance of hydrogen and helium, their crustal budgets remain poorly quantified. This study systematically assesses the accumulation of natural hydrogen and helium in global sedimentary basins by integrating predictive models for both gases with H2/He ratios. The predictive model infers natural hydrogen resources in global sedimentary basins of 100–106 Mt (megatons), with a most probable estimate of 1.7 × 103 Mt, and subsurface helium resources of 17.9 Mt. Water–rock reactions and the decay of radioactive elements within crystalline basement rocks generate natural hydrogen and helium, respectively, supplying background gas fluxes to overlying sedimentary basins. Mantle degassing and source rocks within sedimentary sequences provide supplementary gas contributions, resulting in an underestimation of these resources. This study reveals that global sedimentary basins host significant accumulations of natural hydrogen and helium resources—a finding that warrants increased attention.
